To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the differential impact of the core mathematics intervention on students with different levels of mathematics achievement was mediated by the frequency of teacher delivered, individual student practice opportunities.

(a) students with low initial mathematics skills benefited more from an empirically validated core mathematics program than students with higher initial mathematics skills, (b) this effect was partially explained by the rate in which the program was delivered with fidelity, and (c), the rate in which individual practice opportunities were provided to students explained this effect.
the rate of individual practice opportunities during core instruction was a statistically significant mediator of the differential effectiveness of the program on student achievement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding why some interventions are effective for some students, and not effective for others.
understanding why the effects of core academic instruction are not uniform across different skill-levels.
the question of whether the effects of core instruction are uniform across different skill groups or whether the effects are moderated by student initial achievement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the results of this study provide some support for the notion that the observed instructional components of a core mathematics program for kindergarten students with mathematics difficulties may explain why the program's treatment effect is moderated by students' initial mathematics skills.

the results of this study suggest that the rate of teacher delivered individual student practice opportunities may be an important component of effective core mathematics instruction, and that this component of explicit mathematics instruction may explain why students' initial levels of mathematics achievement were previously found to moderate treatment effects of an empirically valid core mathematics program for kindergarten students with mathematics difficulties.
the results of this study are inconclusive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the rate in with which teachers facilitate individual student practice opportunities in core mathematics classrooms is an important instructional variable for at-risk learners and may help to explain the differential treatment effects of mathematics interventions.
the effects of explicit instruction may not be uniform and that the rate of practice opportunities during instruction may be a mechanism that explains why the effects are not uniform.
the rate at which teachers provided students with practice opportunities during core math lessons was a key factor in the treatment effect of the program for students with mathematics difficulties.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the effects of academic interventions are not uniform across all skill levels in mathematics, and that instructional components of core mathematics interventions may explain the differential effectiveness of such programs.

the differential effectiveness of an empirically tested core mathematics program for students with mathematics difficulties can be explained by the extent to which teachers facilitated individual practice opportunities for students during instruction. (Author abstract)
the rate of individual student practice opportunities is a critical feature of effective mathematics instruction for young children with mathematics difficulties.
